body.statement: Each eligible selector-correction, reachable-fixing, labelled-elimination, and residual-compilation transition preserves the represented observation-target relation on its registered branch domain after composing its emitted circuit, and discharges exactly its displayed polynomial identity or inequality obligation. For every nonhalting transition \(\zeta\Rightarrow\zeta'\), \(\mu_H(\zeta')<_{\mathrm{lex}}\mu_H(\zeta)\): selector correction removes one \(\sigma\)-token, fixing removes one active vertex, elimination removes a nonempty active set or one \(\ell\)-token, and residual compilation removes the sole residual token and enters a terminal state. Therefore the deterministic schedule terminates after finitely many encoded transitions, conditional only on the residual verifier finding a candidate.
body.justification: The calculus is executable only when every scheduled move has a decidable eligibility test, an exact successor, and a local invariant.
body.gap: The anchor algorithm names graphical operations but does not provide a fixed-support retained-image transition semantics with a per-rule decreasing certificate.
body.consumer: A selector-aware implementation can reject malformed transitions and replay every certificate from its encoded state log.
body.proof_tex:
For a state, let its represented relation mean the set of observation--target pairs obtained by recursively evaluating its labelled kernels with primitive parameters in \(\mathcal I_H\) satisfying the current constraint list \(\mathcal J\), on the domain where every registered divisor is positive. Initially this is the normalized relation by \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\).

Consider a selector transition with token \(\sigma=(s,X,r,x_s)\). Eligibility gives \(s\in H\) and says that the stored multiplexer has intervention status one and value \(x_s\) at the labelled occurrence. The multiplexer equation therefore gives
\[
 X=x_s,\qquad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x\}=\mathbf 1\{x_s=x\}
\tag{7}
\]
at that occurrence. Replacing it by \(\mathbf 1\{X=x_s\}\) and evaluating every child at \(x_s\) is thus a polynomial identity modulo the appended gate and coordinate-copy equations. The rewrite adds no divisor. The sole initialization divisor is
\[
 p_H(S=s)=\sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}}p_H(v,s),
\tag{8}
\]
which is precisely the registered selector normalizer. Hence the represented relation is unchanged, and (7)--(8) are exactly the two local obligations displayed for this transition.

For a fixing token \(\varphi=(s,W,D,k)\), eligibility supplies both the reachability condition and the ledger certificate for
\[
 m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}.
\]
On the registered domain \(m_{s,W}>0\). If \(K'_{s,D}=K_{s,D}/m_{s,W}\), then
\[
 m_{s,W}K'_{s,D}=K_{s,D}.
\tag{9}
\]
Thus (9), checked modulo \(\mathcal J\), proves equality of the predecessor and successor kernel descriptions. The separate certified sum--product expression for \(m_{s,W}\) is exactly the positivity obligation. No unregistered division is used.

For a sum-elimination token, finite distributivity proves
\[
 K'=\sum_Z\prod_{k\in L}K_k.
\tag{10}
\]
For a district-elimination token, the fixed topological quotient gives the uniquely ordered product of the proper-district kernels. In either case the verifier cancels common factors, checks (10) or the district identity after cross-multiplication modulo \(\mathcal J\), and checks separately the stipulated factorization of every reduced denominator. Positivity of all factors on the registered domain makes cross-multiplication reversible there. Consequently the represented relation is preserved and the obligations discharged are exactly those in the elimination definition.

At a residual projection, acceptance means that for its candidate \(P/D\),
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0\pmod{\mathcal J},
\tag{11}
\]
and that every factor of \(D\) has a positivity-ledger certificate. Since \(D>0\) on the registered domain, (11) is equivalent there to \(t_{a,H}^N=P(o_H^N)/D\), proving preservation on the formula branch. At a residual contrast, acceptance means that the two affine parameter maps satisfy, identically on their rational box,
\[
 o_H^N(\eta_b^+)=o_H^N(\eta_b^-),\qquad
 t_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^+)-t_{a,H}^N(\eta_b^-)\ne0,
\tag{12}
\]
together with all simplex, strict cell-positivity, and exact-support inequalities. Applying \(\rho_H\) and using normalization equivalence transports (12) to the original observation and target maps. Thus the residual step preserves the represented relation in its asserted formula-or-twin sense and discharges precisely its verifier obligations.

It remains to prove termination. For a selector step, \(|R|\) is unchanged and \(|\Sigma|\) falls by one. For a fixing step, \(|R|\) falls by one, so changes in later coordinates do not matter. For elimination, either a nonempty \(Z\) is removed from \(R\), or the earlier coordinates are unchanged and \(|\mathcal L|\) falls by one. A residual step leaves the earlier coordinates unchanged, lowers \(|\mathcal R|\) from one to zero, and enters a terminal state. Hence every admitted move to a nonterminal successor, and also the final residual move, strictly decreases
\[
 \mu_H=(|R|,|\Sigma|,|\mathcal F|,|\mathcal L|,|\mathcal R|)
\]
in lexicographic order.

This order on \(\mathbb N^5\) is well founded. Indeed, in an infinite strictly decreasing sequence the first coordinate could decrease only finitely often; after it stabilized, the second could decrease only finitely often, and repeating this argument through the fifth coordinate gives a contradiction. Therefore no execution contains infinitely many admitted transitions. If the residual verifier accepts a candidate, its transition consumes the sole residual token and is the scheduled halting move. If it accepts none, the finite execution can instead be stuck; this is precisely the condition stated in the theorem.
